images.alt_grc: ὁ ὅρος ἐπὶ τῇ γῇ κεῖται· ὁ γείτων ὀργίζεται.
images.alt_en: Summer 429, a farm near Acharnae: a toppled boundary stone lies in the grass between two fields; a cut olive tree with its branches on the path; Demokritos stares, and his neighbour Antimachos points at him angrily.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ἀντίμαχος μετὰ δύο μαρτύρων πρὸς τὴν θύραν ἔρχεται.
images.alt_en: A city doorway in Kydathenaion: Antimachos, flanked by two witnesses, calls out the summons; Demokritos listens in the doorway; inside, Ariston and Lysis look up from the table.

images.alt_grc: ἀνὴρ ἐν τῷ δικαστηρίῳ λέγει· «ἐγὼ γάρ, ὦ Ἀθηναῖοι …»
images.alt_en: A speaker in a plain cloak addresses rows of seated jurors; a scroll labelled ΛΥΣΙΟΥ in the corner marks it as a speech written about 400 BC, later than the story.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Ἀρίστων καὶ ὁ Εὔδημος τῷ Δημοκρίτῳ μαρτυρεῖν βούλονται.
images.alt_en: Evening in Ariston's courtyard: Demokritos counts on his fingers who can be a witness; Ariston nods, Eudemos waves his arms eagerly; Syros stands apart by the wall.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σύρος εἶδε τὸν δοῦλον τὸν ὅρον κινοῦντα.
images.alt_en: Syros's memory, in muted colours: at dusk a slave levers a boundary stone out of the ground with a bar while a man in a cloak watches from behind an olive tree.
Ariston stands between Syros and Demokritos with one hand raised, refusing; Chrysis and Elpis watch from the doorway; Syros looks at the ground.

images.alt_grc: οἱ δικασταὶ καθίζονται· ἡ κλεψύδρα ῥεῖ.
images.alt_en: Inside a law court at dawn: several hundred jurors on wooden benches, a magistrate on a platform, and a clay water clock on a stand with water running from its spout into a jar below.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Δημόκριτος λέγει· «ἐγὼ γάρ, ὦ ἄνδρες δικασταί …»
images.alt_en: Demokritos on the speaker's platform, hands open, speaking plainly; Antimachos scowls from the other side; jurors lean forward.
Jurors shout and wave; Demokritos pauses with a small smile; the water in the clock is nearly gone.
Jurors file past two urns on a table, each holding a pebble hidden in his fist; Eudemos among them, a charcoal smudge on his cheek.
Officials tip out the two urns and count pebbles in small heaps; Demokritos and Antimachos watch from either side, tense.

images.alt_grc: τὼ γείτονε τὸν ὅρον αὖθις ἱστάτον.
images.alt_en: Autumn on the farm: Demokritos and Antimachos together set the boundary stone upright again, each with both hands on it; Lysis and Mikion watch; a young olive shoot grows from the cut stump.
A boundary stone (ὅρος): a rough upright slab set in the earth between two fields.
Two farmhouses side by side, a man at each door raising a hand to the other: neighbours.
A law court: rows of jurors on benches, a speaker's platform and a water clock.
A juror: a bearded citizen over thirty, seated, holding a voting pebble and a staff.
A witness raising his hand to speak before the jurors.
A clay water clock: water runs from a spout near the bottom of one jar into another; the speech lasts as long as the water.
A voting pebble held between two fingers; a small heap of pebbles beside it.
A voting urn: a jar with a narrow mouth into which the juror drops his pebble.
The boundary stone of the Athenian Agora, about 500 BC, still standing where it was set; the archaic letters read ΗΟΡΟΣ ΕΙΜΙ ΤΕΣ ΑΓΟΡΑΣ, 'I am the boundary of the Agora'.

A painted clay plaque from Corinth, 6th century BC (Penteskouphia): men digging clay in a pit for a potter's workshop, one passing a basket up, a jug of water hung beside them. Most such labourers were enslaved.

images.alt_grc: ἡ κλεψύδρα ἡ ἐκ τῆς ἀγορᾶς
images.alt_en: The clay water clock found in the Athenian Agora, about 400 BC: a jar with a bronze outlet near the base, inscribed ΑΝΤΙΟΧΙΔΟΣ (of the tribe Antiochis); full, it ran for about six minutes.
Bronze jurors' ballots of the 4th century BC from the Agora: discs with an axle through the centre, some hollow (to condemn) and some solid (to acquit), stamped ΨΗΦΟΣ ΔΗΜΟΣΙΑ, 'public ballot'.
